meta.title: Bengali Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 107 expressions · 57 everyday, 38 idioms, 12 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 107 Bengali set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 57 everyday phrases, 38 idioms and 12 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Bengali → English (see the Bengali, recall the meaning) and English → Bengali (see an English meaning, recall the Bengali) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Bengali A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the levels. The Phrases subdeck holds greetings and wishes of both communities (শুভ সকাল, ঈদ মোবারক, শুভ বিজয়া), the phrasebook sentences a learner needs whole (আপনি কেমন আছেন, আমি বুঝি না, আমার সাহায্য লাগবে), with তুই, তুমি and আপনি where the dictionary gives them, and the set everyday expressions (কিছু না, বার বার, দেখতে পাওয়া); the Idioms are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (ঘোড়ার ডিম, 'a horse's egg', means nothing at all); the Proverbs are complete sayings. WHERE THESE COME FROM: every expression of English Wiktionary's Bengali that no level teaches was read, and these were chosen by hand; compound nouns (bird and plant names, 'laptop computer'), second spellings, personal sentences about one's faith or nationality, partisan slogans, religious formulas in Arabic, and vulgarities were left out. The dictionary's Bengali is small, so this deck is too. Within each subdeck the commonest expressions come first, by a frequency list built from film and television subtitles. Every expression is printed in the Bengali script with Wiktionary's romanisation beneath it. Real example sentences come with 22 of the 107 expressions. Sources. Meanings and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
